```
## Collider flash is caller-driven and the overlay is filterable

`ColliderDebugSystem` exposes two knobs for keeping the overlay readable in a
real level. `Filter` is a `Func<Entity, bool>` over collider entities: null
(the default) draws every one, and a predicate narrows the overlay to the
handful that matter — a tile world has hundreds of baked terrain colliders that
bury the three you are debugging. `Flash(Entity)` blinks one collider's outline
`Color.White` for `FlashSeconds` (0.12 by default), so an event that resolves
inside a single frame is still visible; it is **caller-driven on purpose** —
the system never flashes on its own from `CollisionMessage`. Flash timers age
by `state.Time` at the top of every `Update`, **before** the
`IsEnabled`/`Enabled` early-return, and entries whose entity died or whose
timer ran out are dropped; `Dispose` clears the table.

**Why:** flashing every contact would strobe continuously on the floor and
walls a body rests against, drowning out the one-frame events worth seeing —
so the game names the moments it cares about (damage landing, a trigger
firing) instead. Ageing while muted is what makes the mute honest: a flash
started just before the overlay is toggled off must not still be white when it
comes back on, possibly many seconds later.
**Breaks:** auto-flashing from collision messages makes the overlay a strobe
and hides real events. Ageing flashes *after* the enabled check (or only when
enabled) makes re-enabling show a stale blink pinned at full brightness.
Dropping the dead-entity check leaks recycled `Entity` keys, so a
newly-created entity that reuses the id inherits a phantom flash. Filtering
inside the draw helpers instead of at the query loop still allocates the mesh
lists for colliders nobody asked to see.
**Tests:** `MonoDreams.Tests/Debug/ColliderDebugSystemTests.cs` —
`Filter_Null_DrawsEveryCollider`,
`Filter_NarrowsTheOverlay_ToTheMatchingCollidersOnly`,
`Flash_TurnsTheOutlineWhite_ThenRevertsWhenTheTimerExpires`,
`Flash_AgesWhileDisabled_SoReEnablingShowsNoStaleBlink`,
`Flash_OnADeadColliderEntity_IsDroppedWithoutThrowing`.
**Depends on:** debug — "This module is opt-in; nothing requires it"
(`Flash` bookkeeping runs even when both toggles are off, which is what the
static/instance mute pair is allowed to skip and this is not); collision —
"A collider is its own entity".
```

Immaterial at 0.5 s/2 s. The 4 `Examples.Core` call sites compile unchanged (new ctor params are optional).

Relatedly, two capture instances in one process keep independent counters, so PNG names could in principle collide (same counter + same millisecond); observed non-colliding, and raw mode cannot collide.</result>

## Collider flash is caller-driven and the overlay is filterable

`ColliderDebugSystem` exposes two knobs for keeping the overlay readable in a
real level. `Filter` is a `Func<Entity, bool>` over collider entities: null
(the default) draws every one, and a predicate narrows the overlay to the
handful that matter — a tile world has hundreds of baked terrain colliders that
bury the three you are debugging. `Flash(Entity)` blinks one collider's outline
`Color.White` for `FlashSeconds` (0.12 by default), so an event that resolves
inside a single frame is still visible; it is **caller-driven on purpose** —
the system never flashes on its own from `CollisionMessage`. Flash timers age
by `state.Time` at the top of every `Update`, **before** the
`IsEnabled`/`Enabled` early-return, and entries whose entity died or whose
timer ran out are dropped; `Dispose` clears the table.

**Why:** flashing every contact would strobe continuously on the floor and
walls a body rests against, drowning out the one-frame events worth seeing —
so the game names the moments it cares about (damage landing, a trigger
firing) instead. Ageing while muted is what makes the mute honest: a flash
started just before the overlay is toggled off must not still be white when it
comes back on, possibly many seconds later.
**Breaks:** auto-flashing from collision messages makes the overlay a strobe
and hides real events. Ageing flashes *after* the enabled check (or only when
enabled) makes re-enabling show a stale blink pinned at full brightness.
Dropping the dead-entity check leaks recycled `Entity` keys, so a
newly-created entity that reuses the id inherits a phantom flash. Filtering
inside the draw helpers instead of at the query loop still allocates the mesh
lists for colliders nobody asked to see.
**Tests:** `MonoDreams.Tests/Debug/ColliderDebugSystemTests.cs` —
`Filter_Null_DrawsEveryCollider`,
`Filter_NarrowsTheOverlay_ToTheMatchingCollidersOnly`,
`Flash_TurnsTheOutlineWhite_ThenRevertsWhenTheTimerExpires`,
`Flash_AgesWhileDisabled_SoReEnablingShowsNoStaleBlink`,
`Flash_OnADeadColliderEntity_IsDroppedWithoutThrowing`.
**Depends on:** debug — "This module is opt-in; nothing requires it"
(`Flash` bookkeeping runs even when both toggles are off, which is what the
static/instance mute pair is allowed to skip and this is not); collision —
"A collider IS an entity (colliders-as-entities)".

input.new_string:
**Frame capture.** `ScreenshotCaptureSystem` writes frames to the debug
directory in one of two formats: PNG (encoded off-thread; the right
choice for occasional verification shots, but the ~50 ms encode caps a
per-frame capture at ~15–26 fps) or raw RGBA (`CaptureFormat.Raw` — a
synchronous memcpy dump sustaining full frame rate, ~3.5 MiB per frame
at 1280x720). Off by default. Env-driven capture goes through
`ScreenshotCaptureSystem.FromEnvironment`, the single owner of the
`MONODREAMS_SCREENSHOT=1|png|raw` / `MONODREAMS_SCREENSHOT_INTERVAL` /
`MONODREAMS_SCREENSHOT_MAX_FRAMES` contract; the replay-gated pattern
(`"screenshots": true` in `input_replay.json`) still drives
PNG-interval capture. See the `debug` module's `docs/overview.md`
§ Frame capture for the disk-cost table and the raw-vs-encoded
rationale.

  FromEnvironment as the single owner of the MONODREAMS_SCREENSHOT /

  byte accounting, frame cap and disk-full stop. Demos host composes the

  Flash(entity)/FlashSeconds blinks a collider white so one-frame contacts

  replay — lets an injection channel own the derived cursor positions
  instead of having them clobbered by the per-frame screen→world derivation.

Ports the three self-verification tools proven in the `gmtk-2026gj` build-verify loop back into the engine, so capture that doesn't lie, contacts you can see, and replays that own the mouse become engine equipment.

## 1. Raw frame capture (`debug`)

PNG capture lies about motion: one encode costs ~50 ms against a 16.6 ms budget, MonoGame's fixed timestep responds with four sim updates per draw, and any clip judders — you can't tell a capture artefact from a gameplay bug. `CaptureFormat.Raw` dumps RGBA via `MemoryMarshal.AsBytes` (a memcpy, no encode, zero per-frame allocation, deliberately synchronous), sustaining full frame rate, with byte accounting, a disk-full stop, and a frame cap (3.5 MiB/frame — a 20 s take is ~4.2 GB, so `_MAX_FRAMES` is not optional).

`FromEnvironment` is now the **single owner** of the env contract (`MONODREAMS_SCREENSHOT=1|png|raw`, `_INTERVAL`, `_MAX_FRAMES`) — a second reader of it would be a second dialect. The Demos host composes it after the composite in both headless and windowed runs. `AnnotateFilename` (PNG mode) lets callers stamp game-state into filenames so "find the frame where X happens" becomes an `ls`, not a scrub. `CaptureNow` (the protected deterministic headless path) is byte-for-byte unchanged.

## 2. `ColliderDebugSystem`: `Filter` + `Flash`

The overlay was all-or-nothing — hundreds of baked terrain colliders bury the three you care about. `Filter` is a predicate (null = draw all). `Flash(entity)` blinks a collider white for `FlashSeconds` so a one-frame contact is visible; caller-driven deliberately so resting contacts don't strobe. Flashes age even while the overlay is muted, so re-enabling never shows a stale blink.

## 3. `CursorPositionSystem.SkipDerivation` (`cursor`)

The missing mouse half of input replay: `SkipHardwareRead` lets a replay inject cursor input, but the position system recomputed screen→world each frame and clobbered the injection (including forcing `OutsideViewport = true`). One flag lets the injection channel own the derived positions.

## Docs

- `debug` overview: new **Frame capture** section — env contract table, disk-cost table, and the raw-vs-encoded rationale (raw is the verification tool; encoded clip capture is recorded as future work: MGCB-bundled ffmpeg on desktop, `MediaRecorder` on web — kept out so verification and sharing don't get conflated).
- New premises with real `Tests:` fields: env-contract single ownership, synchronous zero-alloc raw writes, caller-driven flash/filterable overlay, cursor derivation stand-down.
- `CORE_TENETS` §8, `.claude/CLAUDE.md`, and `debug/module.json` refreshed off the stale "PNGs every 2s" description.
- Fixed a `.gitignore` rule (`/MonoDreams.Tests/[Dd]ebug/`) that silently swallowed the new test folder; runtime debug output remains covered by `**/bin/**/debug/`.

## Tests (43 new; full-solution Release gate: 1116 + 47 passed, 0 failed)

- `FromEnvironment` contract: mode selection, defaults (png→0.5 s, raw→every frame), interval override with invariant-culture parsing (asserted under an ambient pt-BR culture), cap parsing, invalid-mode rejection — via a fake `IPlatformServices`.
- Integration (`RawFrameCaptureTests`): 40-frame headless Demos run with cap 25 asserts exactly 25 `.rgba` blobs, contiguous counters (full-rate, no skips), exact 1280×720×4 byte geometry, monotonic game-time in filenames, the cap log line, and the Dispose summary.
- Collider: filter narrows 3→1, flash turns the outline white then reverts on expiry, ages while disabled, dead-entity flash dropped safely.
- Cursor: injected virtual/world/transform state survives the frame under `SkipDerivation`, plus two contrast cases proving derivation still runs (and clobbers) without it.

Deliberately out of scope, as recorded in the issue: encoded clip capture. The raw write-failure (full-disk) branch shares the tested stop mechanism but isn't directly simulated — no in-process `GraphicsDevice` pattern exists in the suite; the premise's `Tests:` field says exactly that.

2	
3	> Technical invariants the engine assumes about the debug overlays
4	> module: `ColliderDebugSystem`, `SpriteDebugSystem`,
5	> `ScreenshotCaptureSystem`, and `SystemProfiler` (per-system frame
6	> timing — not a pipeline system, a plug into `foundation`'s socket).
7	> (The `Logger` and the input-replay
8	> scaffold live in `foundation` because they're useful in production;
9	> this module adds the *visual* debug overlays and screenshot capture
10	> only.) Read this before changing any of those pieces or relying on
11	> the screenshot output for testing — including the headless Demos
12	> observe-and-self-verify path (`MonoDreams.Demos/Game1.cs`,
13	> `HeadlessOptions.cs`), which builds on `ScreenshotCaptureSystem`.
14	> Frame capture has two formats (encoded PNG and uncompressed raw RGBA) and
15	> one environment contract that selects between them — see the "Frame
16	> capture" section of [`overview.md`](overview.md) for the env table and the
17	> disk-cost table those premises refer to.
18	
19	## This module is opt-in; nothing requires it
20	
21	A screen's pipeline assembly never *needs* a debug system. Each system
22	in this module is registered only if the screen explicitly wants it,
23	and each respects a static `Enabled` flag plus an instance `IsEnabled`
24	flag so a registered system can be muted without removing it from the
25	pipeline. Tests and production-bound builds simply omit the
26	registrations.
27	
28	**Why:** the framework-not-library tenet says required behavior lives
29	in `foundation`, optional behavior in its own module. Debug overlays
30	allocate per-frame (transient mesh entities), so making them mandatory
31	would impose a cost on every screen.
32	**Breaks:** if a future refactor moves any of these systems into a
33	required module, every game pays for debug rendering whether they
34	asked for it or not. The static `Enabled` toggles also become global
35	state that's harder to keep off across compositions.
36	**Tests:** none yet.
37	**Depends on:** —
38	
39	## Debug overlays draw via the same `DrawComponent` path as everything else
40	
41	`ColliderDebugSystem` and `SpriteDebugSystem` create ephemeral entities
42	with `DrawComponent { Type = Mesh }` and a high `LayerDepth` (e.g.
43	1.0, 0.98) each frame, then dispose them at the start of the next
44	frame. They do not call `SpriteBatch` directly and they do not fork
45	`MasterRenderSystem`.
46	
47	**Why:** the rendering pipeline's "`MasterRenderSystem` is the sole
48	renderer" premise forbids a second SpriteBatch path. Generating
49	transient mesh entities is the engine-pure way to render overlays.
50	The high layer depth keeps them on top of the rest of the scene
51	without needing a separate target.
52	**Breaks:** if a debug system bypassed `MasterRenderSystem` to draw
53	directly, the next render-target switch would lose the overlay (the
54	SpriteBatch would be in the wrong state) — and the "no parallel
55	renderer" review lens would flag the PR.
56	**Tests:** none yet.
57	**Depends on:** rendering — "`MasterRenderSystem` is the sole renderer";
58	rendering-mesh — "Mesh entities use the same `DrawComponent` slot".
59	
60	## Debug overlays must be prep'd before `MasterRenderSystem` runs
61	
62	`ColliderDebugSystem` and `SpriteDebugSystem` register inside the
63	prep stage (between `SpritePrepSystem` and `MasterRenderSystem` in the
64	reference pipeline at
65	`MonoDreams.Examples/Screens/LoadLevelExampleGameScreen.cs`). They
66	must run before `MasterRenderSystem` so the transient mesh entities
67	are in the world when the renderer iterates draw queries; they should
68	run after `SpritePrepSystem` so the sprite bounds they visualize
69	reflect the same frame's `DrawComponent` data.
70	
71	**Why:** the overlay entities have no draw data until the debug system
72	creates them. If `MasterRenderSystem` runs first, the entities aren't
73	in the world yet and the overlays render one frame late. Likewise,
74	`SpriteDebugSystem` reads `DrawComponent.Position` / `Origin` / `Size`
75	to compute bounds; reading before `SpritePrepSystem` writes those gives
76	stale data.
77	**Breaks:** overlays flicker, lag, or visualize last frame's bounds
78	during camera motion or animation.
79	**Tests:** none yet.
80	**Depends on:** rendering — "Rendering systems run last in the pipeline".
81	
82	## Collider flash is caller-driven and the overlay is filterable
83	
84	`ColliderDebugSystem` exposes two knobs for keeping the overlay readable in a
85	real level. `Filter` is a `Func<Entity, bool>` over collider entities: null
86	(the default) draws every one, and a predicate narrows the overlay to the
87	handful that matter — a tile world has hundreds of baked terrain colliders that
88	bury the three you are debugging. `Flash(Entity)` blinks one collider's outline
89	`Color.White` for `FlashSeconds` (0.12 by default), so an event that resolves
90	inside a single frame is still visible; it is **caller-driven on purpose** —
91	the system never flashes on its own from `CollisionMessage`. Flash timers age
92	by `state.Time` at the top of every `Update`, **before** the
93	`IsEnabled`/`Enabled` early-return, and entries whose entity died or whose
94	timer ran out are dropped; `Dispose` clears the table.
95	
96	**Why:** flashing every contact would strobe continuously on the floor and
97	walls a body rests against, drowning out the one-frame events worth seeing —
98	so the game names the moments it cares about (damage landing, a trigger
99	firing) instead. Ageing while muted is what makes the mute honest: a flash
100	started just before the overlay is toggled off must not still be white when it
101	comes back on, possibly many seconds later.
102	**Breaks:** auto-flashing from collision messages makes the overlay a strobe
103	and hides real events. Ageing flashes *after* the enabled check (or only when
104	enabled) makes re-enabling show a stale blink pinned at full brightness.
105	Dropping the dead-entity check leaks recycled `Entity` keys, so a
106	newly-created entity that reuses the id inherits a phantom flash. Filtering
107	inside the draw helpers instead of at the query loop still allocates the mesh
108	lists for colliders nobody asked to see.
109	**Tests:** `MonoDreams.Tests/Debug/ColliderDebugSystemTests.cs` —
110	`Filter_Null_DrawsEveryCollider`,
111	`Filter_NarrowsTheOverlay_ToTheMatchingCollidersOnly`,
112	`Flash_TurnsTheOutlineWhite_ThenRevertsWhenTheTimerExpires`,
113	`Flash_AgesWhileDisabled_SoReEnablingShowsNoStaleBlink`,
114	`Flash_OnADeadColliderEntity_IsDroppedWithoutThrowing`.
115	**Depends on:** debug — "This module is opt-in; nothing requires it"
116	(`Flash` bookkeeping runs even when both toggles are off, which is what the
117	static/instance mute pair is allowed to skip and this is not); collision —
118	"A collider IS an entity (colliders-as-entities)".
119	
120	## `ScreenshotCaptureSystem` is gated by `IsEnabled` set from `input_replay.json`
121	
122	`ScreenshotCaptureSystem` is disabled by default. The integration test
123	pattern is to write `"screenshots": true` into `debug/input_replay.json`
124	and have the screen set `screenshotSystem.IsEnabled = replayPlan?.Screenshots
125	?? false` after constructing the system. Production builds either omit
126	the registration or leave `IsEnabled = false`.
127	
128	**Why:** capturing PNGs of the backbuffer every 2 seconds allocates,
129	hits the disk, and stalls the render thread briefly. Default-off keeps
130	the cost out of any session that didn't explicitly ask for it. The
131	replay file is the natural carrier of "this run wants screenshots"
132	intent — it already lives in the debug dir.
133	**Breaks:** a screenshot system that captured unconditionally would
134	slow every run by a few % and fill the debug directory with stale
135	PNGs. The opt-in pattern keeps the system free in normal use.
136	**Tests:** none yet (the integration-test screens follow the pattern,
137	but no test asserts that `IsEnabled = false` produces no PNG output).
138	**Depends on:** foundation — "`Logger` requires `Initialize` before any
139	write" (screenshots respect `MONODREAMS_DEBUG_DIR` the same way logs

  "postInstallNotes": "## debug installed

Add whichever you need to your pipeline:

- `ColliderDebugSystem(world, camera)` — draws AABB / SAT outlines after rendering.
- `SpriteDebugSystem(world, camera)` — draws sprite bounds and pivot points.
- `ScreenshotCaptureSystem(graphicsDevice, intervalSeconds, debugDir, format, maxFrames)` — frame capture: PNG (occasional verification shots) or raw RGBA (full-rate 60 fps takes). Env-driven runs use `ScreenshotCaptureSystem.FromEnvironment(...)` — the single owner of the `MONODREAMS_SCREENSHOT` / `_INTERVAL` / `_MAX_FRAMES` contract (see `docs/overview.md` § Frame capture). The replay-gated pattern (`"screenshots": true` in `debug/input_replay.json`) still works for PNG-interval capture.

**Per-system profiling (`SystemProfiler`).** Not a pipeline system — a static that plugs into `foundation`'s socket. Wire it in the host:

1. At boot, `SystemProfiler.Enabled = PlatformServices.Current.GetEnvironmentVariable("MONODREAMS_PROFILE") == "1";` — the setter installs `SystemProfiler.Record` as `GatedSystem.TimingSink`, so with the env var unset nothing is installed and the cost is one null check per gated system per frame.
2. In the host's `Update` loop, `SystemProfiler.CountFrame();` then `SystemProfiler.ReportPeriodically(state, ref timer);` (a `float` field on the host; the interval is `SystemProfiler.ReportInterval`, 2s by default).

Every gate a screen registers through `EditorPipelineRegistrar` carries the entry's full hierarchical registration name, so report rows read `logic.game` / `logic.game.enemies` — groups nest under their own total. Reports go through `Logger`, which reaches the browser console on a web head.

**Replay testing.** `Logger` and the replay scaffold live in `foundation` because they're useful in production. This module adds the *visual* debug overlays and the profiler — they're safe to ship in dev builds and exclude in release.

See `docs/premises.md` for the module's invariants and `docs/overview.md` for the full tour.",
  "premisesRef": "docs/premises.md"
}

80	- **Web** — `canvas.captureStream()` + `MediaRecorder`. The browser encodes the canvas natively; an engine-side encoder would be strictly worse and would need a filesystem the platform doesn't have (which is also why the Demos host builds its env capture under `#if !MONODREAMS_WEB`).
81	
82	## Cross-module dependencies
83	
84	- `rendering` — overlays draw through `DrawComponent` and `MasterRenderSystem`; screenshots capture the backbuffer.
85	- `collision` — `ColliderDebugSystem` reads `BoxColliderComponent` and `ConvexColliderComponent` to know what to outline.
86	- `foundation` — `SystemProfiler` plugs into `GatedSystem.TimingSink` and reports through `Logger`. The arrow points this way only: `foundation` defines the socket and never references this module.
87	
88	## Extension points
89	
90	- **New debug overlays.** Follow the pattern of the existing two systems: create transient `DrawComponent { Type = Mesh }` entities each frame at a high `LayerDepth` (so they render on top), dispose them at the start of the next frame, and ship a static `Enabled` flag plus an instance `IsEnabled` flag. Never call `SpriteBatch` directly.
91	- **HUD overlays (FPS, entity count, draw call count).** Same pattern with `DrawComponent { Type = Text }` on a HUD target. Aspirational direction list.
92	- **Capture-on-exit screenshot.** Mode where `ScreenshotCaptureSystem` guarantees one final PNG at game shutdown — useful for replay post-mortems. Aspirational direction list.
93	
94	## See also
95	
96	<<<<<<< HEAD

file.content:
- **Web** — `canvas.captureStream()` + `MediaRecorder`. The browser encodes the canvas natively; an engine-side encoder would be strictly worse and would need a filesystem the platform doesn't have (which is also why the Demos host builds its env capture under `#if !MONODREAMS_WEB`).

## Cross-module dependencies

- `rendering` — overlays draw through `DrawComponent` and `MasterRenderSystem`; screenshots capture the backbuffer.
- `collision` — `ColliderDebugSystem` reads `BoxColliderComponent` and `ConvexColliderComponent` to know what to outline.
- `foundation` — `SystemProfiler` plugs into `GatedSystem.TimingSink` and reports through `Logger`. The arrow points this way only: `foundation` defines the socket and never references this module.

## Extension points

- **New debug overlays.** Follow the pattern of the existing two systems: create transient `DrawComponent { Type = Mesh }` entities each frame at a high `LayerDepth` (so they render on top), dispose them at the start of the next frame, and ship a static `Enabled` flag plus an instance `IsEnabled` flag. Never call `SpriteBatch` directly.
- **HUD overlays (FPS, entity count, draw call count).** Same pattern with `DrawComponent { Type = Text }` on a HUD target. Aspirational direction list.
- **Capture-on-exit screenshot.** Mode where `ScreenshotCaptureSystem` guarantees one final PNG at game shutdown — useful for replay post-mortems. Aspirational direction list.
